one_line: A player can use the 'tweak' emote to spend stamina and make their character visibly spasm and shake for a few seconds.
player_facing_mechanics: Triggers the tweak component on the living mob for 8 seconds
Carbon users must pay 60 stamina via adjustStaminaLoss; if they cannot, the emote aborts with no effect
The affected atom visually shakes by animating pixel_x/pixel_y in one of four random cycles for the duration
The effect stops early if the mob dies (COMSIG_LIVING_DEATH)
Mobs at stat > SOFT_CRIT (dead/gibbed/etc.) cannot receive the component
Brute, non-living but otherwise valid atoms can also be given the component when instantiated directly with a time
data_only_parts: the four hardcoded pixel-offset animation keyframe sequences are pure animation data
logic_parts: tweak/process() applying the cycling animate() pixel_x/pixel_y offsets
tweak/Initialize() eligibility checks (isliving stat > SOFT_CRIT guard, isatom guard, COMPONENT_INCOMPATIBLE)
signal registration/cleanup on death and Destroy() teardown
run_emote() stamina gating and conditional component attachment
byond_specific: animate() with pixel_x/pixel_y, time and loop arguments (BYOND screen-space animation)
port_notes: An SS14 port needs an ECS component marking the entity as tweaking plus a system that periodically jitters its SpriteOffset (or a sprite animation), a timer for the duration, and a death event handler to cancel it; the emote maps to an action/chat emote plus a stamina system DoAfter-style check. BYOND's chained animate() pixel offsets have no direct equivalent and must be re-authored as either a keyframe SpriteOffset animation or a repeating timer-driven offset system. A human must decide whether tweaking is player-visible/networked, whether it should be an Action (cooldown-free emote) or a chat emote, if the 60-stamina cost maps to SS14's stamina system, and whether the remaining frames are worth replicating exactly.
